session.assistantText:
Workspace is nearly empty (`README.md` only, no commits), so the concrete job here is capability probing plus picking the strongest judging route. I will probe the advertised routes before committing to one.
One probe failed before finishing. Let me check the others.
Both `deepseek-account` routes failed. Waiting on the two magpie routes.
Two magpie routes answered; both `deepseek-account` routes failed before finishing, so that provider is unusable here. Now I hand the real work to the strongest judging route.
Executor dispatched on the selected route. Waiting for its artifact.
The goal was capability probing for this repo, and the smallest change that meets it is one new record file plus a pointer line, which is what landed.

**Route selection.** I probed all four advertised routes at their highest advertised effort, `max`, with one identical non-tool task that had an underspecified premise.

| Route | Probe at max | Status |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `deepseek-account/deepseek-flash` | no closing message | unavailable this session |
| `deepseek-account/deepseek-v4-pro` | no closing message | unavailable this session |
| `magpie/workbuddy/deepseek-v4.1-flash` | answered, applied formula as written | available |
| `magpie/workbuddy/minimax-m3.1-flash` | answered, flagged the formula | available |

The selected route is `magpie/workbuddy/minimax-m3.1-flash` at reasoning effort `max`. It is the strongest route available here, and there is no stronger one to escalate to. The two `deepseek-account` routes failed outright at max, so they were excluded as unavailable rather than ranked as weaker. Between the two magpie routes the arithmetic was identical at `E[N] = 11.24`, so arithmetic could not separate them. The tie broke on judgment. The minimax route noticed the supplied formula is not a standard `M/G/c` form, listed the readings of the summation index, and computed the Erlang C result `E[N] = 4.32`. The v4.1-flash route accepted the premise silently. For a repo whose work is judgment about capability, that difference decides it.

The failure of the `deepseek-account` routes is a session-scoped observation, not a property of the provider. The artifact says so and says to re-probe before relying on either.

**What changed.** [CAPABILITY.md](CAPABILITY.md) is new and holds the route table, the selection, the reason the loser lost, and four re-verification steps. [README.md](README.md) gained one link line and kept its original two lines. Nothing else was touched. No commits, branches, or remotes were created.

**For the next maintainer.** The re-verify steps are written to be rerunnable as-is. They name the registry listing tool and the per-route probe, and they state the two things to record per child, which is whether it closed and whether it challenged the formula. The one judgment the executor made that the brief left open was how to phrase the probe task in those steps, since the original prompt text was not handed down. It described the task by its discriminating property instead of quoting it, so a re-verifier knows what the task must do without a false exactness.

One caveat worth your attention. The probes ran at `max` only. The artifact claims effort `max` because it is the highest advertised and nothing cheaper was shown sufficient, but no cheaper effort was actually tested, so the doc does not claim a lower effort would fail. If that boundary matters later, the probes need to be repeated downward.
